text: The bay lies flat and warm, close to its annual high, the water giving back heat it has been storing since May. Along the wet margins of every drainage ditch between Bay City and Caseville, joe-pye weed stands head-tall, its dusky-rose crowns drawing the last of the tiger swallowtails. Goldenrod has opened along the roadsides, and the season has crossed into gold. After dark, katydids have taken up their dry rasping in the oaks, a sound that belongs to August and to no other month. On the AuSable, trico spinners are falling in the early morning above the riffles. The whitetail bucks in the alder thickets are still in velvet, but the days are already shorter than they were, and the first warblers will be moving within the month.
